answer: Random jury of 9 drawn per round at the wharf node pool without replacement. A farm holding k% of identities lands a full jury only k^9 of the time; at k=20% that's 5e-7, a hard river of failed rounds. Each thread of collusion must sustain 1/k^8 redundant identities per verdict to break even, so latency-bound attackers bleed stake faster than honest nodes. This works because the exponential k^9 penalty makes jury capture cost grow far faster than any linear identity budget.
